clusters.state_of_play: Explosions reported in Kyiv after Zelenskyy warned of a Russian massive attack planned over several days; Russia has now struck Ukrainian cities with missiles, drones, and glide bombs, killing at least 10 civilians. North Korean ballistic missiles were used in strikes on Zaporizhzhia, killing seven civilian workers at the Metinvest steel plant and injuring 21; three more civilians including a 15-year-old boy were killed by Russian drones and artillery. Zelenskyy also warns Putin will use the Russian election — in which opposition to the war is banned — as a pretext for a major troop call-up. Russia's Supreme Court has now banned the country's only anti-war party from next month's parliamentary elections, the latest move to silence dissent. Ukraine is also targeting Wildberries, a Russian retail giant akin to Amazon, as part of an effort to bring the sense of war home to the Russian population. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) warns that Putin is preparing to use this winter to break Kyiv, and will not enter serious negotiations if he believes he has a viable military path. Separately, Putin has ordered a probe following the humiliation of Russia's Navy Day parade. Russia has released former US Marine Robert Gilman, 32, after more than four years in prison; Putin granted a humanitarian pardon and Trump is credited with securing the release. The State Department stated explicitly that no prisoner exchange took place and Washington made no concessions. Fox News had framed the release as a prisoner exchange, which the US government has now denied. Gilman had been in a dissociative stupor for 47 days and was gravely ill; his father disputes the Russian account of his arrest. Trump has signed an executive order overhauling the childhood vaccine schedule, drawing pushback from doctors, pharma, and public health experts. A 7.4-magnitude earthquake — Colombia's strongest on record — has struck western Colombia, killing at least 240 people and leaving more than 3,000 missing; rescuers are racing to find survivors amid fears the death toll will rise steeply. A 32-year-old woman was pulled alive from a collapsed apartment on Tuesday, and footage circulating on social media shows a baby being rescued from the rubble of a destroyed building in Cali. The Trump administration has pledged $15.5 million in relief.

On the earnings call, Zuckerberg outlined a broad AI strategy covering enterprise (agents, APIs, compute, internal software) and personal AI agents acting on users' behalf. The results came despite a media blitz including a WSJ op-ed published the prior day in which Zuckerberg touted AI's positive effects. Separately, CoreWeave reported Q2 revenue of $2.58B, up 112% YoY, beating estimates, with a $104B backlog and 1.5 GW of contracted power, sending CRWV shares up ~10-11% after hours, though the company carries $35B in debt. In unrelated political news, Sabato's Crystal Ball has shifted Ohio Rep. Max Miller's reelection race to a toss-up, with Democrats and the Blue Dog Action Fund now treating him as a genuinely vulnerable incumbent worth serious investment. In a separate media-industry story, the Paramount-Skydance merger with Warner Bros. Discovery is under intensifying legal and political pressure: California AG Rob Bonta is pursuing a multi-state antitrust lawsuit, prompting Skydance CEO David Ellison to threaten moving Paramount out of California if Bonta won't negotiate a settlement. Bonta has said he believes Paramount is eager to settle and has held private conversations with Governor Gavin Newsom about the case. Paramount's top lawyer stated the company is happy to cooperate with oversight, while Democratic lawmakers are readying aggressive oversight of the deal.

clusters.state_of_play: Explosions reported in Kyiv after Zelenskyy warned of a Russian massive attack planned over several days; Russia has now struck Ukrainian cities with missiles, drones, and glide bombs, killing at least 10 civilians. North Korean ballistic missiles were used in strikes on Zaporizhzhia, killing seven civilian workers at the Metinvest steel plant and injuring 21; three more civilians including a 15-year-old boy were killed by Russian drones and artillery. Zelenskyy also warns Putin will use the Russian election — in which opposition to the war is banned — as a pretext for a major troop call-up. Russia's Supreme Court has now banned the country's only anti-war party from next month's parliamentary elections, the latest move to silence dissent. Ukraine is also targeting Wildberries, a Russian retail giant akin to Amazon, as part of an effort to bring the sense of war home to the Russian population. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) warns that Putin is preparing to use this winter to break Kyiv, and will not enter serious negotiations if he believes he has a viable military path. Separately, Putin has ordered a probe following the humiliation of Russia's Navy Day parade. Russia has released former US Marine Robert Gilman, 32, after more than four years in prison; Putin granted a humanitarian pardon and Trump is credited with securing the release. The State Department stated explicitly that no prisoner exchange took place and Washington made no concessions. Fox News had framed the release as a prisoner exchange, which the US government has now denied. Gilman had been in a dissociative stupor for 47 days and was gravely ill; his father disputes the Russian account of his arrest. Trump has signed an executive order overhauling the childhood vaccine schedule, drawing pushback from doctors, pharma, and public health experts. A 7.4-magnitude earthquake — Colombia's strongest on record — has struck western Colombia, killing at least 240 people and leaving more than 3,000 missing; rescuers are racing to find survivors amid fears the death toll will rise steeply. A 32-year-old woman was pulled alive from a collapsed apartment on Tuesday, and footage circulating on social media shows a baby being rescued from the rubble of a destroyed building in Cali. The Trump administration has pledged $15.5 million in relief.
